title: An explicit operator lane is never silently overridden
description:
Five signed-in-only commands set PAPYRUS_GRAPHQL_AUTH=user in code (references_search_cli.py references search, references_titles.py repair-titles, references_transcripts.py capture-transcripts, references_thumbnails.py capture-thumbnails, monitoring_view_cli.py monitors), so an operator's explicit --auth iam (or env iam) is quietly overridden. They must refuse with a message when the explicit lane is iam and the command needs the signed-in lane, and otherwise run signed in. Depends on PR #1517 (PPY-5f119a). Gherkin required.

Feature: An explicit operator lane is never silently overridden
  Scenario Outline: A signed-in-only command given the operator lane
    When I run <command> with --auth iam
    Then it refuses before reading or writing anything
    And the message says this command needs the signed-in lane and to run papyrus login <site> or drop --auth iam
    And it exits non-zero
    Examples: references search, references repair-titles, references capture-transcripts, references capture-thumbnails, monitors
  Scenario: The env var names the operator lane
    Given PAPYRUS_GRAPHQL_AUTH=iam
    When I run any of the five commands
    Then it refuses with the same message
  Scenario: No lane named
    Given a signed-in session and no lane named
    When I run any of the five commands
    Then it runs as the signed-in user and the process environment is not rewritten
  Scenario: Explicit user lane
    When I run one of them with --auth user
    Then it runs signed in
